body:
Runner rule (Termal::Opus3, 2026-10-30, after Greg's TermAl restart at ~05:58Z). My remote runner chains were launched as `ssh host '… script …; cut log | head'` from Claude background Bash tasks on Central. A Central restart kills those ssh sessions. In this case the full gates on DL560 and Windows B survived, because their scripts wrote everything to files. But my Mac WAITER for the next queued leg died, so that leg never started. A second waiter survived with a dead stdout pipe, and could have died on its next echo by SIGPIPE, partway through launching a leg.
Rule: launch every remote chain DETACHED on the host, `nohup bash SCRIPT > LOG 2>&1 < /dev/null &`, with all progress written to files there. Keep Central's background ssh only as a read-only waiter that loops on the host until a marker appears and then prints the log. Losing it loses nothing. After a restart, recover by reading host files and processes (pgrep, logs, run dirs). Never relaunch a leg that has a run dir; start only legs that never began.
